**Feijóo Tries to Resolve Valencia Crisis Amid Tensions with Vox**
Alberto Núñez Feijóo, leader of the Spanish People's Party (PP), faced one of his most challenging days as opposition leader on November 3, 2025, amid a deepening crisis in the Valencia region. Santiago Abascal of Vox openly blamed Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez for the disaster, criticizing the PP for failing to defend its own, worsening relations between the two right-wing parties. Vox sources stated they would not support any candidate who does not meet their conditions, referencing Extremadura’s early elections. Potential successors include María José Catalá, the mayor of Valencia (and a member of parliament), and Juan Francisco Pérez Llorca, the PP valencian secretary general, but not Vicente Mompó, who is not a member of parliament. This crisis marks Feijóo’s first major confrontation with a regional baron, highlighting tensions dating back to Mazón’s early 2023 coalition with Vox, which many in Génova blamed for the PP’s poor performance in the July 2023 general election. The situation may define the future of the PP’s internal dynamics and its relationship with Vox.

**The PP-Vox Relationship Hits Breaking Point, Foreshadowing an Early 2026 Electoral Cycle**

The rift, which intensified in autumn 2025, stems from disagreements over coalition governance in Aragón and Extremadura, where both parties failed to pass budgets due to open conflict. Vox’s leader, Santiago Abascal, is reportedly considering blocking Javier Azcón’s candidacy for future investiture, citing betrayal over the dismissal of a racist and antisemitic Vox advisor. In Extremadura, regional PP leader María Guardiola, initially critical of Vox, was forced into a coalition after the 2023 regional elections, but relations have deteriorated further. A major point of contention is the PP’s shift on immigration policy under Alberto Núñez Feijóo, whose recent Barcelona plan—featuring point-based visas, deportation of criminal immigrants, stricter nationality rules, and cuts to the Ingreso Mínimo Vital (IMV)—is seen by Vox as copying their own platform. Tensions escalated in Congress when PP deputy Cayetana Álvarez de Toledo accused Minister Félix Bolaños of ‘feeding’ Vox, implying a secret alliance between the PSOE and Vox, a claim denied but widely circulated.
